**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/07/21 (Fri) 22:46
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Archimedes was a Greek mathematician and inventor from the city of Syracuse.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Archimedes made important contributions to mathematics and physics, including calculating the ratios of the volumes of a sphere and its inscribed cylinder and cone, and determining the quadrature of parabolic segments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Archimedes wrote about the principles of buoyancy and leverage and introduced an abstract number system to express large numbers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Archimedes was known for his practical insights and was well-regarded by the Roman upper class, who saw the value of mathematics and physics in military applications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Archimedes was killed during the Roman conquest of Syracuse, but he remains a revered figure in the history of mathematics.
- [USER] Mathematics within Christian philosophy.
- [USER] The fall of the Roman empire implied that Greek manuscripts became buried in the libraries of small monasteries.
- [USER] The number of people being able to read Greek diminished.
- [USER] The pax romana had secured a wide spread of Greek philosophy, and of Greek philosophical manuscripts, and although it had reached only a tiny part of the population, it was kept alive, in a way.
- [USER] Geometria and arithmetica, even if mostly viewed practical or mystical, had been a part of Roman culture.
- [USER] The early Christians distanced themselves from the pagan Greek philosophers.
- [USER] The ideas behind the Greek world order were not consistent with the notion of an omnipotent God.
- [USER] The new Christian ideas proved to be much more supportive for mathematical practices, since the Christian God was a deity who favoured rules and laws, instead of the irrational and quarrelling gods of the antique civilisations.
- [USER] The divine rules and laws reflected favourably upon the ideas within geometria or arithmetica.
- [USER] Although there was no systematic use of mathematical knowledge within theology, there were several of the old Christian thinkers who tried to connect the two fields.
- [USER] One of the reasons for the popularity of Saint Augustine (354 - 430) was the fact that he was autodidact.
- [USER] Augustine was not versed in the Greek philosophers, which made him the ideal icon to the young religion.
- [USER] Later generations would consider Augustine one of the church fathers, although he had been quite profane in his youth.
- [USER] Augustine did not write about either geometria nor arithmetica, but he was impressed by the possibilities these subjects seemed to offer.
